activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today I am going to explain a routine but very important construction process that you regularly practise in Construction Technology.
This process is scaffolding inspection and preparation.
Although it is routine work, it must be done carefully and in the correct order, because unsafe scaffolding can cause serious accidents on site and place workers at risk.
First, you have to inspect the ground condition where the scaffold will be erected, because unstable ground can cause the scaffold to tilt or collapse.
Before placing any components, the surface should be firm and level.
Then, you have to check the base plates and sole boards to ensure they are positioned correctly.
After that, you have to examine the scaffold frames for visible damage so that defective parts are not used.
You also have to confirm that all components match the required height and load capacity.
You shouldn’t assemble the scaffold at this stage, because inspection must be completed before erection begins.
Careful inspection reduces the risk of structural failure.
Once the inspection is complete, you have to arrange the scaffold components in the correct order to allow smooth assembly.
Then, you have to position the vertical frames properly, because correct alignment ensures stability.
After that, you have to fix cross braces securely so that the scaffold remains rigid and stable during use.
You also have to install guardrails and toe boards to prevent falls and falling objects.
Workers are not allowed to climb the scaffold yet, because final safety checks are still required.
Proper preparation ensures safe working conditions at height.
Finally, you have to recheck all connections to confirm that bolts and couplers are tight.
Then, you have to inspect the working platform to make sure it is level and secure.
After that, you have to place safety tags clearly to indicate the scaffold status.
You also have to inform the site supervisor before use so that approval is recorded.
You shouldn’t load materials onto the scaffold immediately, because permission must be given after inspection.
Following this sequence helps prevent accidents and ensures site safety.
